lines: Linear probing spans layer-wise classifiers~\cite{alain2017understanding}, sentence probing~\cite{conneau2018probing}, and surveys~\cite{belinkov2019analysis,belinkov2022probing,rogers2020primer}; causal abstraction~\cite{geiger2023causal} grounds use of internal representations. Control tasks~\cite{hewitt2019control} distinguish structure from memorization (adopted in \cref{app:control}); \citet{levinstein2024liedetector} raise concerns about spurious correlations that our controls address. Information-theoretic and causal formulations address probe complexity~\cite{voita2020information,pimentel2020information,ravfogel2020null,ravfogel2022rlace,belrose2023leace,elazar2021amnesic}.\footnote{The Tuned Lens~\cite{belrose2023tunedlens} assumes next-token prediction, misaligned with binary CP classification.} Non-uniform layer-wise information distribution~\cite{tenney2019bert,jawahar2019bert,marks2024geometry} and cross-layer disagreement~\cite{kaya2019shallow,zhou2020bert} are well established; we repurpose these for safety probe layer selection (\cref{sec:layer-sensitivity}). Our contribution is that the known layer-wise gradient interacts with metric choice to produce systematic selection bias. \citet{boxo2025linear_probes} show probes can rely on textual evidence; our analysis provides a complementary geometric mechanism at shallow layers. Concurrent works confirm layer sensitivity in related settings: influence estimation~\cite{vitel2025layer}, reasoning dynamics monitoring~\cite{chrabaszcz2026monitoring}, hallucination detection~\cite{alvarez2026transport_geometry}, truth encoding trajectories~\cite{damirchi2026truth}, selective probes~\cite{meyoyan2026bertology}, and multi-layer ensembling~\cite{pais2026linear_probe_scaling}.\looseness=-1

+Recent work addresses layer selection by aggregating across layers. CLAP~\citep{clap2025} uses cross-layer attention over all layers' activations, bypassing single-layer selection for response-level hallucination detection; however, its token$\times$layer joint sequence scales linearly with CoT length, limiting applicability to variable-length reasoning traces. \citet{meyoyan2026bertology} propose a two-stage aggregator (within-layer pooling, then cross-layer aggregation) and find safety-relevant features distributed across multiple layers---directly echoing our observation that different metrics select different layers (\cref{sec:layer-results}). \citet{kim2025layer_deficiency} show layer-wise information content varies non-monotonically, corroborating our layer-dependent findings. These multi-layer approaches complement our diagnostic: we identify the mechanism (cosine compression $\to$ metric bias) that makes single-layer readout unreliable; they propose architectural solutions.\looseness=-1

BOCPD~\cite{adams2007bayesian} detects abrupt distributional shifts; CCS~\cite{burns2023discovering} discovers latent truth directions; RepE~\cite{zou2023representation} identifies concept directions. We adapt all three to temporal commitment detection (\cref{sec:negative}): BOCPD/CUSUM fail on gradual transitions, CCS misaligns temporally, and RepE is model-dependent (BA 0.756 vs.\ 0.559). These failures motivate supervised probes with principled layer selection.\looseness=-1

lines: -Crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility,tab:r18b_full_layer}): its shallow preference is an artifact of cosine compression inflating threshold crossings, while threshold-based deep preference reflects genuine separability~\citep{tenney2019bert}; random-label controls confirm this distinction (\cref{app:random_cp}). C1 is observed across all four studied models (three Qwen-family, one Llama; cross-dataset: \cref{app:advbench_layer_bias}; geometric: \cref{app:cosine_volatility}; split-half: \cref{app:split_half}). The geometric precondition extends to Gemma-2 (standard full attention) but is absent in Gemma-4 (mixed sliding/full attention; \cref{app:gemma_cross_arch}). Annotation noise (${<}2.5$pp BA; \cref{tab:cp_perturbation}) does not threaten C1. Type~I risk from ${\sim}$2{,}240 configurations is bounded by the two-stage design and large effect sizes ($d$ 0.58--2.37; \cref{app:effective_tests}). C2 (HS advantage) is confirmed at 7--8B: nested CV validates the precision gap (10/10 folds, +20--22pp), and residualized HS advantage survives both linear and quadratic position controls (\cref{app:position_residual}). At 32B, C2 is exploratory: $n{=}19$--$20$ precludes nested CV, QwQ-32B's advantage is absorbed by quadratic position, and R1-32B's residualized gap falls below MDE. The association between cosine compression and crossing-rate inflation is correlational; a causal test (e.g., whitening shallow representations) is future work. \textbf{Practical mitigation.} We propose a three-level defense against metric-induced layer selection bias (\cref{app:practical_mitigation}), from minimal (dual metric-family reporting) to robust (three-layer ensemble; $p \leq 0.002$, \cref{tab:ensemble}).\looseness=-1

76	\paragraph{Position mediation.} Position ($t/T$) accounts for 9--20pp of balanced accuracy,\footnote{R1-32B's 20.4pp drop reflects $W{=}1$; at $W{\geq}3$, drops are 9--17pp.} but all models retain non-positional signal above chance (all $p{<}0.001$; \cref{app:position_residual}). Three of four models retain significant non-positional HS advantage (residualized gap +3.7 to +6.9pp, HB corrected); R1-32B's gap is +1.9pp ($p{=}0.914$, $n{=}20$), well below the MDE of ${\sim}$9pp and thus indistinguishable from zero at current power. Quadratic residualization (adding $(t/T)^2$) is computed for all four models: 2/4 retain significance (R1-8B +10.3pp, OT-7B +9.8pp, both HB), while R1-32B (0.0pp) and QwQ-32B ($-$1.0pp) do not (\cref{tab:position_quadratic}). QwQ-32B's HS advantage is fully absorbed by the quadratic position term, meaning the information captured by the probe overlaps substantially with non-linear position. Temporal windowing reduces position dependence (\cref{sec:temporal}).\looseness=-1
77	
78	\enlargethispage{7\baselineskip}
79	\paragraph{Caveats.} Nested 5-fold CV confirms the HS precision advantage for both 7--8B models (10/10 folds; \cref{app:nested_cv}), with shrinkage of 13--25\% relative to holdout estimates. OT-7B nested CV selects L21--27 vs.\ holdout L16 vs.\ CR-composite L0; the +21.9pp holdout estimate is an upper bound. R1-32B achieves significance only at $W{=}1$ with 25\% coverage; at $W{\geq}3$, dimensionality prevents significance. QwQ-32B HS lead time is negative ($-$1.2 to +1.9 steps). False alarm rates remain 11--50\%, so current methods characterize the phenomenon rather than constitute production detectors. Per-model details in \cref{sec:32b-analysis}.\looseness=-1
80

lines: \paragraph{Position mediation.} Position ($t/T$) accounts for 9--20pp of balanced accuracy,\footnote{R1-32B's 20.4pp drop reflects $W{=}1$; at $W{\geq}3$, drops are 9--17pp.} but all models retain non-positional signal above chance (all $p{<}0.001$; \cref{app:position_residual}). Three of four models retain significant non-positional HS advantage (residualized gap +3.7 to +6.9pp, HB corrected); R1-32B's gap is +1.9pp ($p{=}0.914$, $n{=}20$), well below the MDE of ${\sim}$9pp and thus indistinguishable from zero at current power. Quadratic residualization (adding $(t/T)^2$) is computed for all four models: 2/4 retain significance (R1-8B +10.3pp, OT-7B +9.8pp, both HB), while R1-32B (0.0pp) and QwQ-32B ($-$1.0pp) do not (\cref{tab:position_quadratic}). QwQ-32B's HS advantage is fully absorbed by the quadratic position term, meaning the information captured by the probe overlaps substantially with non-linear position. Temporal windowing reduces position dependence (\cref{sec:temporal}).\looseness=-1

\paragraph{Caveats.} Nested 5-fold CV confirms the HS precision advantage for both 7--8B models (10/10 folds; \cref{app:nested_cv}), with shrinkage of 13--25\% relative to holdout estimates. OT-7B nested CV selects L21--27 vs.\ holdout L16 vs.\ CR-composite L0; the +21.9pp holdout estimate is an upper bound. R1-32B achieves significance only at $W{=}1$ with 25\% coverage; at $W{\geq}3$, dimensionality prevents significance. QwQ-32B HS lead time is negative ($-$1.2 to +1.9 steps). False alarm rates remain 11--50\%, so current methods characterize the phenomenon rather than constitute production detectors. Per-model details in \cref{sec:32b-analysis}.\looseness=-1

input.old_string: Crossing rate reverses the central finding via shallow-layer compression (\cref{app:cosine_volatility,tab:r18b_full_layer}): its shallow preference is an artifact of cosine compression inflating threshold crossings, while threshold-based deep preference reflects genuine separability~\citep{tenney2019bert}; random-label controls confirm this distinction (\cref{app:random_cp}). C1 is observed across all four studied models (three Qwen-family, one Llama; cross-dataset: \cref{app:advbench_layer_bias}; geometric: \cref{app:cosine_volatility}; split-half: \cref{app:split_half}). The geometric precondition extends to Gemma-2 (standard full attention) but is absent in Gemma-4 (mixed sliding/full attention; \cref{app:gemma_cross_arch}). Type~I risk is bounded by large effect sizes ($d$ 0.58--2.37; \cref{app:effective_tests}). C2 (HS advantage) is confirmed at 7--8B: nested CV validates the precision gap (10/10 folds, +20--22pp), and residualized HS advantage survives both linear and quadratic position controls (\cref{app:position_residual}). At 32B, C2 is exploratory: $n{=}19$--$20$ precludes nested CV, QwQ-32B's advantage is absorbed by quadratic position, and R1-32B's residualized gap falls below MDE. lines: \paragraph{Position mediation.} Position ($t/T$) accounts for 9--20pp of balanced accuracy,\footnote{R1-32B's 20.4pp drop reflects $W{=}1$; at $W{\geq}3$, drops are 9--17pp.} but all models retain non-positional signal above chance (all $p{<}0.001$; \cref{app:position_residual}). Three of four models retain significant non-positional HS advantage (residualized gap +3.7 to +6.9pp, HB corrected); R1-32B's gap is +1.9pp ($p{=}0.914$, $n{=}20$), well below the MDE of ${\sim}$9pp and thus indistinguishable from zero at current power. Quadratic residualization (adding $(t/T)^2$) is computed for all four models: 2/4 retain significance (R1-8B +10.3pp, OT-7B +9.8pp, both HB), while R1-32B (0.0pp) and QwQ-32B ($-$1.0pp) do not (\cref{tab:position_quadratic}). QwQ-32B's HS advantage is fully absorbed by the quadratic position term, meaning the information captured by the probe overlaps substantially with non-linear position. Temporal windowing reduces position dependence (\cref{sec:temporal}).\looseness=-1

\paragraph{Caveats.} Nested 5-fold CV confirms the HS precision advantage for both 7--8B models (10/10 folds; \cref{app:nested_cv}), with shrinkage of 13--25\% relative to holdout estimates. OT-7B nested CV selects L21--27 vs.\ holdout L16 vs.\ CR-composite L0; the +21.9pp holdout estimate is an upper bound. R1-32B achieves significance only at $W{=}1$ with 25\% coverage; at $W{\geq}3$, dimensionality prevents significance. QwQ-32B HS lead time is negative ($-$1.2 to +1.9 steps). False alarm rates remain 11--50\%, so current methods characterize the phenomenon rather than constitute production detectors. Per-model details in \cref{sec:32b-analysis}.\looseness=-1

lines: -We address the ARR Responsible NLP Research requirements below.

-    \item \textbf{Potential risks:} This research analyzes jailbreak traces to understand how reasoning models commit to generating harmful content. We do not develop new attack methods or release jailbreak prompts. All analyzed content comes from the publicly available HarmThoughts benchmark. We acknowledge a dual-use concern: safety probes that detect commitment could in principle be used to craft reasoning traces that evade detection. We believe the defensive value of understanding commitment dynamics outweighs this risk, as evasion requires white-box access to the probe, which a deployed monitoring system would not expose.

-    \item \textbf{Computational budget:} Our experiments involve 4 models with 209, 228, 100, and 95 traces respectively (632 total), using linear probes and single-layer GRUs. Total compute is minimal (under 4 GPU-hours on a single RTX A6000). No large-scale pretraining or finetuning was performed.

-    \item \textbf{Data:} We use HarmThoughts, a publicly available benchmark with step-level safety annotations, and AdvBench~\citep{advbench} for cross-dataset geometric validation. No new data collection was performed.
-    \item \textbf{Human subjects:} No human subjects research was conducted.
-    \item \textbf{Reproducibility:} All hyperparameters are reported in \cref{app:gru_details,app:bocpd_config}. Code and corrected data will be released upon publication.
